div.p: This Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) Implementation Guide (IG) is designed to facilitate a standardized and secure exchange of healthcare information in Botswana; specifically the handling of laboratory orders in both OpenMRS and PIMS systems to and from the National laboratory system: IPMS. The guide is crafted for Botswana's Health Information Exchange (HIE) and provides a structured approach to managing patient data and laboratory orders.

The goal of this IG is to ensure that laboratory data, including test results, specimen information, and diagnostic reports, can be efficiently exchanged and integrated within the Botswana healthcare setting.
This IG outlines the specific profiles to implement Botswana's LAB-EMR data exchange.
This IG implements FHIR bundles that support conditional patient creates and/or updates:

ul.li: Create: Only create the patient in the Client Registry (CR) if no matches are found for a given business identifier.
Update: Instead of creating a new patient in the CR, ONLY update the administrative information for the patient matching the given business identifier.

div.p: This aims to reduce duplication of patient records and maintain patient data integrity across integrated systems.

div.p: This FHIR IG provides guidance on how to apply FHIR profiles to Botswana's laboratory workflow, ensuring that laboratory systems and EMRs can communicate and share data in a standardized and consistent manner.

While this implementation guide and the underlying FHIR are licensed as public domain, this guide may include examples making use of terminologies such as LOINC, SNOMED CT and others which have more restrictive licensing requirements. Implementers should make themselves familiar with licensing and any other constraints of terminologies, questionnaires, and other components used as part of their implementation process. In some cases, licensing requirements may limit the systems that data captured using certain questionnaires may be shared with.
